title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 7 — WORLD 5: C1 CRITICAL THINKING & ACADEMIC ENGLISH
description: A C1 academic communication world focused on critical reading, evidence evaluation, analytical reasoning, structured argument, source synthesis, and precise academic language.

targets.vocabulary: 3500+ active words with academic collocations, abstract vocabulary, reporting verbs, and discipline-sensitive language
targets.reading: 2000–2500 words with argument mapping, inference, evaluation, synthesis, and rhetorical analysis
targets.listening: 20–25 minutes of lectures, interviews, panel discussions, and academic-style explanations
targets.speaking: 25–30 minutes of seminar discussion, explanation, argumentation, and evidence-based response
targets.writing: 700–900 words with thesis development, source integration, evaluation, cohesion, and academic register
targets.presentation: 12–15 minute evidence-based presentation with structured Q&A

grammar: Advanced nominalization and academic noun phrases
Complex passive and reporting structures for source-based writing
Participle and reduced clauses for information density
Inversion and fronting for rhetorical emphasis
Advanced conditionals for hypothetical and counterfactual analysis
Modal perfects and epistemic modality for evidence and inference
Cohesion through substitution, ellipsis, reference, and lexical chains
Concession, qualification, comparison, and synthesis structures
Hedging and boosting in academic claims
Register control between conversational, academic, and professional English

missions.title: Academic Vocabulary Forge
missions.focus: abstract vocabulary, collocations, nominalization, and reporting verbs
missions.challenge: Upgrade everyday explanations into precise academic English without making them unnecessarily complex.

missions.title: Argument Mapping Lab
missions.focus: claims, reasons, evidence, assumptions, and conclusions
missions.challenge: Identify the logical structure of a complex argument and reconstruct it clearly.

missions.title: Evidence Detective
missions.focus: evidence quality, relevance, reliability, and limitations
missions.challenge: Distinguish strong support from weak, irrelevant, or insufficient evidence.

missions.title: Inference Engine
missions.focus: deduction, implication, probability, and cautious interpretation
missions.challenge: Draw justified conclusions while separating what is known from what is inferred.

missions.title: Source Reporting Mastery
missions.focus: reporting verbs, attribution, paraphrase, and source integration
missions.challenge: Present another person's ideas accurately while maintaining clear source attribution.

missions.title: Counterargument Architect
missions.focus: concession, rebuttal, qualification, and alternative perspectives
missions.challenge: Acknowledge a credible opposing view and respond to it with evidence-based reasoning.

missions.title: Academic Cohesion Lab
missions.focus: reference chains, transitions, lexical cohesion, and paragraph progression
missions.challenge: Build paragraphs that connect ideas smoothly without repetitive linking words.

missions.title: Claim Strength Controller
missions.focus: hedging, boosting, certainty, and academic caution
missions.challenge: Match the strength of a claim to the strength of the available evidence.

missions.title: Bias & Framing Mission
missions.focus: framing, loaded language, omission, perspective, and rhetorical choices
missions.challenge: Explain how wording and selection of information can influence interpretation.

missions.title: Seminar Intelligence Arena
missions.focus: academic discussion, questioning, clarification, challenge, and synthesis
missions.challenge: Join a seminar discussion by developing ideas, asking useful questions, and responding to disagreement.

missions.title: Comparative Reading Lab
missions.focus: cross-text comparison, agreement, disagreement, tone, and evidence
missions.challenge: Compare two complex texts and explain where their reasoning converges and diverges.

missions.title: Lecture Listening Core
missions.focus: main claims, supporting details, examples, signposting, and speaker stance
missions.challenge: Extract the structure and key reasoning from an extended academic-style talk.

missions.title: Thesis Builder
missions.focus: research questions, thesis statements, scope, and argumentative direction
missions.challenge: Turn a broad topic into a focused, defensible central claim.

missions.title: Source Synthesis Workshop
missions.focus: multiple-source integration, comparison, paraphrase, and synthesis
missions.challenge: Combine information from several sources without producing a disconnected summary.

missions.title: Academic Presentation Lab
missions.focus: evidence sequencing, visual explanation, signposting, and Q&A
missions.challenge: Present an evidence-based position clearly and defend it under questioning.

missions.title: Problem-Solving Conference
missions.focus: analysis, alternatives, criteria, recommendations, and decision language
missions.challenge: Evaluate competing solutions and communicate a reasoned recommendation.

missions.title: Science, Technology & Society
missions.focus: complex issues, uncertainty, evidence, ethics, and public communication
missions.challenge: Discuss a technology or science-related issue while distinguishing evidence from speculation.

missions.title: Research Communication Mission
missions.focus: academic writing, professional explanation, summaries, and audience adaptation
missions.challenge: Convert complex research information into a clear explanation for different audiences.

missions.title: World 5 Critical Thinking Marathon
missions.focus: integrated academic reading, listening, speaking, writing, grammar, and vocabulary
missions.challenge: Analyze sources, form a position, defend it orally, and produce a coherent written synthesis.

missions.title: WORLD 5 MASTER QUEST — C1 CRITICAL THINKING
missions.focus: full-world academic mastery assessment
missions.challenge: Demonstrate independent C1 reasoning and communication through evidence-based academic and real-world tasks.

realWorldScenarios: Comparing two reports that reach different conclusions about the same issue
Participating in a seminar and challenging an argument respectfully
Writing a recommendation based on several sources
Explaining research findings to a general audience
Evaluating evidence before making a professional decision
Giving a presentation and defending conclusions during Q&A

assessment.format: Integrated C1 critical-thinking and academic English assessment
assessment.masteryGoal: Learner can evaluate information, construct and defend nuanced arguments, synthesize sources, and communicate complex ideas accurately in C1 academic and professional English.
